title: Build-vs-buy: define Lab Tracker responsibility boundaries vs existing tools
description: Lab Tracker's durable product is the PROV-O / JSON-LD semantic provenance spine threading questions -> notes -> sessions -> datasets -> analyses -> claims -> visualizations (see src/lab_tracker/provenance.py). It is anchored by two node types no external tool provides: Questions (broad-to-atomic inquiry structure) and Claims (epistemic layer linking evidence to conclusions with confidence). Many adjacent responsibilities are either commodity infrastructure or owned by mature tool categories that Lab Tracker risks accidentally half-reimplementing: identity/RBAC, byte/asset storage, data versioning, experiment tracking, note capture (ELNs), transcription, and search. This epic decomposes the boundary decisions: for each adjacent responsibility decide offload / integrate-via-adapter / build-in-house, so effort concentrates on the irreducible semantic core. Already-resolved boundaries: voice transcription is offloaded to an explicit note-scoped action (retained-v1); multimodal note-to-graph extraction is offloaded to the LLM while the human-gated draft->commit diff stays in-house; semantic/vector search is explicitly deferred in retained-v1.
design: Shared principle - pointer-not-reimplementation: for each adjacent responsibility, store a reference (URI + content hash) to the external tool's artifact PLUS the semantic edges the external tool does not model (which question a dataset addresses, which claim an analysis supports). Do not reimplement the external tool's core. The PROV-O export is the integration seam: ingest external artifacts (DVC/DataLad manifests, MLflow runs, ELN entries) as PROV entities and connect them to inquiry and claims. Integrate decisions should strengthen the core by letting it focus on the semantic graph, not shrink it. Danger zone: each integrate decision is a slippery slope toward rebuilding half of MLflow or half of an ELN - resist field-by-field creep past a reference + edges.
acceptance_criteria: Each child decision reaches a recorded outcome (offload / integrate-via-adapter / build-in-house / defer) with rationale, a concrete integration seam or boundary description, and follow-up implementation issues filed where needed. The retained-v1 surface doc (docs/retained-v1-surface.md) and architecture notes are updated to reflect chosen boundaries. Tool-landscape names are validated as current before committing to any one.
close_reason: Completed build-vs-buy boundary epic: all six child decisions recorded and closed, follow-up adapter/storage issues filed, retained-v1 and internal boundary docs updated, PROV-O ingestion seam implemented with dataset external-artifact round-trip coverage, pytest and Ruff passed.

title: Make request lifecycle context-managed
description: Replace finish_request(committed=...) and middleware-level mutable commit flags with a context-managed request lifecycle. The current caller must remember whether a database session committed before deferred after-commit or after-rollback hooks run, which is easy to misuse on exception or rollback paths.
design: Introduce a request-scope/context-manager API that owns repository binding, commit/rollback outcome, deferred-action dispatch, and cleanup. The FastAPI database middleware should enter the request scope, run the handler, commit or roll back through one explicit lifecycle path, and let the scope fire after_commit only after a successful commit and after_rollback only on rollback/error. Keep public route and LabTrackerAPI behavior unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: finish_request(committed=...) is removed or reduced to a non-public compatibility shim that no caller must use. Middleware no longer tracks a mutable committed flag to decide deferred hooks. after_commit hooks run only after a successful commit; after_rollback hooks run on rollback/error paths. Route/session tests cover successful commit and rollback/error behavior. Backend tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented context-managed request lifecycle; removed finish_request(committed=...) and middleware committed flag; added exception rollback hook regression coverage. Gates: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest tests/test_db_wiring.py -q (6 passed), .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest -q (262 passed), .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m ruff check . (passed).

title: test_project_collaboration: order-dependent failures in full pytest run
description:
Two tests in tests/test_project_collaboration.py fail when run as part of the full suite but pass in isolation, suggesting test-ordering or shared-state pollution (e.g. global registry, on-disk artifact, or auth-token cache leaking between tests).

Failing tests (in full-suite run):
- tests/test_project_collaboration.py::test_project_membership_scopes_reads_and_contributor_notes
- tests/test_project_collaboration.py::test_contributor_submits_graph_change_set_for_admin_review

Symptom: POST /notes by 'undergrad'-role user returns 401 Unauthorized (expected 201). Assertion site: tests/test_project_collaboration.py:138.

Repro:
  .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest -q                          # both fail (246 passed, 2 failed)
  .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest tests/test_project_collaboration.py -q   # both pass

First observed on commit f99d1b5 ((feat): retire in-memory API runtime, prescribed by bead lab-tracker-0if.1), which retired the in-memory store and rewrote service-layer auth-context handling across many service modules. Likely related to that teardown — probably an earlier test in the suite mutates shared state (a process-global auth/session cache, env var, or sqlite file) that the membership tests then read as the wrong identity.

Suggested investigation:
1. Run pytest with -p no:randomly (if applicable) and bisect: 'pytest tests/test_X.py tests/test_project_collaboration.py' for each X to find the polluting test.
2. Look for module-level state in the modified services from f99d1b5 (analysis/claim/dataset/note/project/question/session/visualization/graph_draft services) — anything that caches auth context or DB sessions across requests.
3. Check tests/api_helpers.py (new in f99d1b5) for fixtures that might leave state behind.

Likely owner: same author/agent who landed lab-tracker-0if.1, since the failure surface aligns with that change.
close_reason: Could not reproduce after claiming: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest -q passed with 248 passed in 94.03s. Closing as no longer active; reopen with a fresh repro order if it returns.

title: Move lab-tracker skill into repo with generated API reference
description:

Current pain: external skill prose has described question payloads as title/broad/atomic while the live API requires text and one of descriptive | hypothesis_driven | method_dev | other. It has also missed live validation constraints such as pagination limit 200, causing agents to discover schema mismatches by failed POSTs in each new consumer repo.
design:
Store the skill source at skills/lab-tracker/SKILL.md or another repo-owned path with a clearly marked generated section. Add a generator/check that reads the live OpenAPI schema, preferably via create_app().openapi() in-process so CI does not require a running server, and rewrites or validates the API field names/enums section. Keep narrative workflow guidance human-editable while deriving schema-specific field names, enum values, and constraints from OpenAPI.

Publishing/syncing to Sam's local skills directory or other skill-distribution mechanism can be handled by the implementation if appropriate.
acceptance_criteria: The lab-tracker skill source lives in this repo. API field/enums guidance is generated from OpenAPI rather than handwritten and includes current retained-v1 field names, enum values, and important constraints for projects, questions, notes, sessions, datasets, analyses, claims, visualizations, graph drafts, and pagination where relevant. A CI-friendly test/check fails if the generated section drifts from OpenAPI. Updating a Pydantic schema or enum causes the next skill generation/check to surface the new field/enum without a manual prose edit. Backend gates pass.

title: Make Lab Tracker MCP config portable
description:
Make Lab Tracker MCP configuration portable for consumer repos. The working v0 .mcp.json in LiteratureEmbeddings used a hardcoded absolute path to the lab-tracker .venv Python executable, which breaks across machines and clones.

Consumers need a canonical .mcp.json snippet that does not require per-machine editing.
design: Support one or both portable launch paths: an environment-variable based command such as ${LAB_TRACKER_PYTHON:-python}, or an installed lt-mcp console entrypoint that imports/runs the existing MCP server. The MCP server must remain API-backed and must not write directly to the database. Preserve python -m lab_tracker.mcp_server as a compatibility path.

Existing MCP tests pass. The lab_tracker init scaffolder can emit a generated .mcp.json that works after normal package installation or with a documented LAB_TRACKER_PYTHON/LAB_TRACKER_VENV environment variable.

title: Package lab_tracker_client consumer helpers
description:
Add a supported Python consumer package named lab_tracker_client, or a clearly supported vendored single-file client under clients/python, so downstream repos can import Lab Tracker helpers instead of copying scripts/lt.py.

Minimum public surface: LabTracker client class, EntityRef helper, upsert_project, upsert_question, upsert_note, quick_capture, and list_* helpers for retained-v1 entities needed by consumer repos. This package should replace the ~250-line LiteratureEmbeddings scripts/lt.py HTTP client/idempotency/CLI implementation.
design:
Prefer a small public API backed by HTTP calls to the existing Lab Tracker API. Keep auth/base-url configuration explicit and environment-friendly. Implement canonical idempotency keys: project by name, question by text within project, note by first non-blank line marker. Match the live OpenAPI enum values, and raise a typed LTValidationError or equivalent on bad enum values so consumers do not maintain shadow enum sets.

Include a compatibility shim pattern so a consumer repo scripts/lt.py can collapse to a one-line re-export from lab_tracker_client. Consider an lt console entrypoint for health, ids, note, quick, list-questions, and list-notes commands if it fits the packaging surface.
acceptance_criteria: lab_tracker_client is importable from this package or from clients/python. It exposes LabTracker, EntityRef, upsert_project, upsert_question, upsert_note, quick_capture, and list_* helpers. Idempotency by project name, question text, and note first-line marker is implemented and tested. Bad enum values fail client-side with a typed error informed by the OpenAPI schema or generated constants. A consumer scripts/lt.py can re-export the client helpers without duplicating logic. Backend tests and ruff pass.
close_reason: Implemented lab_tracker_client with LabTracker, EntityRef, idempotent project/question/note upserts, quick_capture multipart helper, list_* helpers, env-configured module-level shims, enum validation, and tests. title: Replace LabTrackerAPI service mixins with composed services
description: Replace the LabTrackerAPI inheritance facade with explicit service objects while preserving the current flat LabTrackerAPI public method surface. The current class inherits many service mixins that implicitly share repository, raw storage, and request context through self, which hides dependencies and makes service-level unit testing difficult.
design: Introduce a ServiceContext that carries the active repository/unit-of-work, raw storage, request context, and any shared service helpers. Convert *ServiceMixin classes into normal service classes that receive this context and any explicit service dependencies via constructors. LabTrackerAPI remains a thin compatibility facade exposing the existing flat methods used by routes, MCP paths, and tests; it delegates internally to composed services. Split singleton/root API construction from request-scoped API construction where practical so repository/request-context availability is enforced by types or constructors instead of runtime optional checks. Replace lambda-passing repository writes with an explicit unit-of-work/context-manager style in the new services rather than carrying _run_repository_write(lambda repository: ...) forward.
acceptance_criteria: Service dependencies are explicit in constructors instead of hidden through mixin inheritance. LabTrackerAPI continues to expose the current flat method names and existing route/MCP behavior remains unchanged. Request-scoped and singleton/root construction paths are represented by distinct types or otherwise made explicit. Representative services can be unit-tested without instantiating the full facade. New service write paths use an explicit unit-of-work/context-manager pattern rather than lambda-passed repository operations. Backend tests pass.
close_reason: Composed LabTrackerAPI services behind the flat facade; converted service mixins to explicit services with ServiceContext/unit_of_work; added service composition tests. Gates: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest tests/test_service_composition.py -q (4 passed), .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest -q (266 passed), .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m ruff check . (passed).

title: Retire dual in-memory/repository runtime
description: Remove the parallel InMemoryStore path and make LabTrackerAPI/service reads and writes use the repository path unconditionally. The current dual runtime keeps a dict-backed store and SQLAlchemy repository active in the same process, forcing every read/write through cache/repository branching and whole-store hydration after failed writes.
design: Delete InMemoryStore, hydrate_from_repository, _uses_in_memory_entity_cache, _get_cached_entity, and repository/store branching from API and services. Tests that need fast feedback should use repository-backed SQLite fixtures rather than the parallel dict store. Preserve the retained-v1 public behavior and API method names while simplifying persistence internally.
acceptance_criteria: No parallel dict store remains in runtime code. Reads and writes go through LabTrackerRepository-backed persistence. Existing API behavior is unchanged for retained-v1 workflows. Tests that previously depended on InMemoryStore use repository-backed fixtures. Backend tests pass.
close_reason: Repository-only LabTrackerAPI runtime implemented; in-memory store removed and tests migrated to SQLite repository helper.

title: Decision: offload auth/RBAC instead of maintaining bespoke identity

Candidates: FastAPI-Users (library altitude, likely sweet spot for single-lab deploys), or an IdP such as Keycloak/Authentik (self-host) or Clerk/Auth0 (SaaS) if multi-tenant. Decide whether to offload and at what altitude (library vs service).
design: Apply pointer-not-reimplementation: Lab Tracker keeps project membership/role edges (which user has which role on which project) in the graph, but delegates credential storage, session/token issuance, and the device grant to the chosen provider/library. Avoid running a full IdP unless multi-tenant requirements justify the operational weight.
acceptance_criteria: Recorded decision (offload-to-library / offload-to-IdP / keep-bespoke-with-rationale). If offloading: a migration sketch for existing UserModel/DeviceToken data and a mapping of project roles onto the provider. Operational cost noted for single-lab installs.

title: Split decision context assembly into focused modules
description: Decompose decision_context.py into focused modules. The current decision-context assembly is large enough to obscure separate responsibilities such as querying graph data, selecting relevant records, compacting payloads, and shaping the MCP decision-context response.

acceptance_criteria: Representative decision-context outputs remain stable for retained-v1 use cases. title: Add lab_tracker init consumer scaffolder
description:
Add an lt setup or lab_tracker init command that scaffolds Lab Tracker integration files into any consumer repository in one step.

The LiteratureEmbeddings setup required hand-written scripts/lt.py, .mcp.json, AGENTS.md Lab Tracker guidance, and lt_ids-style state. New consumers should start with those files generated from Lab Tracker-owned templates.
design:
Implement a console entrypoint, e.g. lab_tracker init [--target REPO_PATH] [--project-name ...]. Generate .mcp.json using the portable MCP launch path, scripts/lt.py as a thin re-export from lab_tracker_client, AGENTS.lt.md or an AGENTS.md fragment documenting the three-mechanism decision tree, and lt_ids.json as a placeholder or project-name-driven bootstrap output.

Keep scaffolding idempotent: do not overwrite local changes without an explicit force flag, and report created/skipped files. The AGENTS fragment should distinguish MCP for lightweight reads, script/client upserts for substantive notes, and CLI for terminal scratch work, and it should document the canonical first-line-marker idempotency pattern.
acceptance_criteria: mkdir new-project; cd new-project; lab_tracker init produces a repo state with portable .mcp.json, scripts/lt.py, AGENTS.lt.md or AGENTS fragment, and lt_ids.json. python -m scripts.lt health succeeds when Lab Tracker is reachable and configured. Generated files use lab_tracker_client and portable lt-mcp/LAB_TRACKER_PYTHON wiring rather than absolute local paths. The command is idempotent and has tests for create, already-exists, and force/overwrite behavior. Backend tests and ruff pass.

description: Centralize project-scoped authorization instead of sprinkling role, project lookup, and contributor checks across service methods. The current pattern relies on each method remembering the right preamble.

Services should depend on the policy and call named policy methods for read/write/review actions. Avoid decorator-only enforcement as the primary abstraction.
acceptance_criteria: Representative project read/write/review checks go through one policy surface. Services no longer open-code the common role/project/contributor preamble where the policy applies. Regression tests cover allowed and denied access for representative workflows, including leakage prevention.
close_reason: Centralized project authorization in ProjectAuthorizationPolicy, wired it through LabTrackerAPI, ProjectService, NoteService, and GraphDraftService while preserving existing behavior. Added policy and composition tests; filed follow-up lab-tracker-sbo for least-privilege write tightening. title: Move request validation into Pydantic schemas where practical
description: Move service-level request validation into Pydantic create/update schemas where practical. Validation such as non-empty fields, metadata normalization, file-list normalization, and claim confidence currently lives partly in services and partly in schemas, making the trust boundary fuzzy.
design: Use Pydantic v2 field validators/model validators on request schemas where the rule belongs to input validation. Keep service-level checks for rules that require repository lookups, permissions, status transitions, or cross-entity invariants. If this touches shared helper cleanup together with status transition work, coordinate with that bead.
acceptance_criteria: Invalid request payloads fail at the schema boundary where applicable. Service methods no longer duplicate schema-only validation. Existing invalid-payload tests pass or are updated to assert schema-level errors. Backend tests pass.
close_reason: Moved practical request-shape validation into Pydantic schemas: nonblank string validators, duplicate UUID-list checks, and note metadata normalization. Regenerated the Lab Tracker skill API reference. Service guardrails remain for direct API and repository/domain-context checks. Gates: schema/reference focused tests (6 passed), full pytest (295 passed), Ruff (passed).

title: Genericize status transition validation
description: Replace duplicated status-transition helper functions with a generic transition validator. Question, dataset, session, analysis, and claim status checks currently repeat the same shape with different enum tables.
design: Introduce a generic helper that accepts the current enum value, next enum value, and transition table. Preserve current allowed transitions and error wording unless a test intentionally updates the wording.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicated status-transition functions are removed or reduced to thin wrappers. Question, dataset, session, analysis, and claim transition behavior is unchanged. Relevant transition tests pass.
close_reason: Reduced duplicated status transition helpers to thin wrappers over a generic transition validator while preserving current error messages and behavior. Gates: focused transition/service tests (16 passed), full pytest (291 passed), Ruff (passed).

title: Decide whether the three-representation model layer is earning its keep
description: Make an explicit design decision for whether Lab Tracker should keep paying the cost of separate domain models, SQLAlchemy ORM models, Pydantic schemas, and hand-written mappers. The current architecture is clean, but the three-representation model creates a large maintenance multiplier and the mapper layer must be updated manually for each field.
design: Evaluate the full representation strategy, not just mapper boilerplate: keep separate domain/ORM/schema layers, collapse domain and ORM with SQLAlchemy 2.0 typed models plus Pydantic from_attributes, adopt SQLModel, derive schemas from domain/ORM models, or generate mapper boilerplate. Record the chosen path and rationale in the bead before broad implementation. Use one pilot entity to prove persistence behavior, validation/wire behavior, migration cost, and test strategy before spawning broader implementation beads.
acceptance_criteria: The bead records a concrete written direction for domain models, ORM models, Pydantic schemas, and mapper responsibilities, including why the chosen tradeoff is worth it for retained-v1. One pilot entity demonstrates the chosen approach without regressing persistence or API behavior. Follow-up implementation beads are created for wider migration or cleanup if needed. Backend tests relevant to the pilot pass.
notes:
2026-05-28 representation decision for retained-v1:

Keep the three explicit representations for now. Domain models remain the service/repository contract and the place where retained-v1 domain fields are expressed without SQLAlchemy session behavior leaking upward. SQLAlchemy ORM models remain persistence-only database rows. Pydantic schemas remain the HTTP/MCP wire/input boundary rather than being generated from ORM models during retained-v1.

Do not collapse to SQLAlchemy-as-domain, SQLModel, or generated schemas in this phase. Those options could delete code, but they would also couple route payload shape, persistence mapping, and migration details during an active architecture cleanup. The safer tradeoff is to keep the boundary and reduce its maintenance cost.

Mapper responsibility stays explicit but should move from one monolithic sqlalchemy_mappers.py file into focused aggregate/entity modules with narrow tests and a compatibility barrel for existing imports. The pilot entity is Project: extract Project mapping into a focused mapper module, wire repository persistence through it, preserve the old import surface, and cover mapper plus project persistence/API behavior. Follow-up work should split the remaining mapper groups in the same style.
close_reason: Recorded retained-v1 representation decision to keep domain/ORM/schema boundaries, extracted Project mapper as the pilot with compatibility re-exports, wired project repository to the focused mapper, and filed follow-up lab-tracker-0la for remaining mapper groups. Gates: tests/test_sqlalchemy_mappers.py and project repository CRUD (7 passed), project HTTP CRUD route (1 passed), full pytest (281 passed), Ruff (passed).

title: Split MCP server into client, tool modules, and registration entrypoint
description: Split the large MCP server module into the API HTTP client, grouped MCP tool modules, and a small registration/entrypoint layer. The current file combines auth retry client behavior, many MCP tool definitions, schema helpers, and module startup.
design: Create a client module for HTTP/auth/retry behavior, grouped tool modules by aggregate or workflow, and a server/entrypoint module that registers tools. Preserve the API-backed boundary: MCP tools call the Lab Tracker API and do not write directly to the database.
acceptance_criteria: python -m lab_tracker.mcp_server still starts the MCP server. Existing MCP tests pass. Tool payload and response behavior is unchanged. No direct DB writes are introduced.
close_reason: Split MCP server into API client, grouped tool modules, resource registration, and a thin entrypoint while preserving tool behavior.

Avoid broad constructor rewiring until the service-composition direction is stable; low-risk pure extraction can start earlier.

title: Preserve uploaded source-file metadata for graph drafting
description: Uploaded photos, audio, and files that enter the staged preproposal review path need source-file metadata so AI graph draft proposals can reason about when and how the artifact was captured. Add upload-time metadata for filename, MIME type, size, checksum, storage timestamp, and client-supplied created/last-modified timestamps; make mobile capture send browser file timestamps when available; ensure graph-draft context carries the metadata.

title: One-tap phone pairing: QR + auto-submit + reachable URLs
description:
The pairing flow shipped under lab-tracker-bbd works but has three manual steps that defeat the 'no friction' goal: the enrollment URL contains the laptop's origin (often 127.0.0.1, not phone-reachable), there's no QR code so the user has to ferry the URL manually, and the phone shows a label form before pairing.

This bead replaces all three with: server renders a phone-reachable enrollment URL (resolved from request.base_url, overridable via LAB_TRACKER_PUBLIC_BASE_URL); the enrollment response includes an inline-SVG QR code of that URL; the DevicesPage shows the QR prominently next to the copy-URL fallback; the EnrollPage auto-submits with a User-Agent-derived label as soon as it loads, so scanning the QR ends in 'paired and in capture' with one tap.
design: Use segno for QR rendering (pure-Python, SVG-native, no Pillow dep). Determine base URL preference order: explicit setting, then request.base_url, then a hostname warning. EnrollPage keeps a manual override path (?label=foo) so the user can pair multiple phones distinguishably if needed, but defaults to UA-derived label.
acceptance_criteria:
- /auth/devices/enrollment returns enrollment_url that points to the request's external host, not 127.0.0.1
- LAB_TRACKER_PUBLIC_BASE_URL setting overrides the derived host (for tunnels, prod)
- Response includes enrollment_qr_svg containing valid SVG QR encoding the enrollment URL
- DevicesPage renders the QR inline; copy-URL is the fallback
- EnrollPage auto-submits on load, no label form required, label sourced from User-Agent
- End-to-end smoke: scan QR on iPhone Camera, tap pop-up, lands at /app/capture as paired device with no further taps
close_reason: Closed

title: Batch draft service: persist proposals + retry/dead-letter
description:
Service-level orchestration that ties together build_batch_graph_context (lab-tracker-jdy) and the pluggable draft_from_batch client (lab-tracker-641). Given a set of staged notes, it builds the context packet, calls the configured client, persists the resulting proposal set as a pending batch with full traceability back to the source notes, and handles model failures with bounded retries + a dead-letter record so the runner can surface them.

Splits out of lab-tracker-641 once the provider abstraction and the OpenAI client method landed; persistence touches the data model (GraphChangeSet currently ties to a single source note and needs either schema extension or a sibling BatchGraphDraft entity) and warrants its own commit and review pass.
design: Decide: extend GraphChangeSet to carry a list of source_note_ids, or introduce BatchGraphDraft wrapping multiple GraphChangeSets/change-set-equivalents. Either way, every operation in the persisted record must trace back to the note(s) that motivated it via existing source_refs. Retries: bounded (e.g. 3) with exponential backoff for transient HTTP errors; non-retryable validation failures go straight to dead-letter. Dead-letter is a persisted record with the failure category, error text, and the offending input so a human can inspect.
acceptance_criteria:
- create_batch_graph_draft(notes, *, user_hint=None, actor=None) on the service layer
- Persists a pending batch with operation-level traceability to source note ids
- Retries transient model errors with bounded attempts + backoff
- Dead-letter record on terminal failure with category, error, and input snapshot
- Tests cover: success path persistence, retry on transient error, dead-letter on terminal error, empty-batch short-circuit

title: Implement decision-context MCP tooling for assistant clients
description: Implement the product spec in docs/mcp-decision-context-tooling.md: add a read-only decision-context API/MCP tool, expose retained-v1 low-level read tools for datasets/analyses/claims/visualizations and provenance, add consultation policy resource, update AGENTS/skill instructions, and test task-kind validation, graph context retrieval, truncation, ambiguity, and read-only behavior.

The spec should define trigger policy, task kinds, read-only context APIs, response schema, integration with AGENTS/skills, acceptance criteria, and non-goals.

title: Batch review UI: approve/reject daily proposal sets
description:
Extend the existing graph-draft review card pattern (referenced in commit 502390c) to a batch container. The user sees today's pending batch as a single review session: a list of proposed operations with per-item accept / reject / edit, plus 'approve all' / 'reject all' shortcuts.

Approved operations commit through the existing graph mutation path. Rejected and edited operations are recorded for future model feedback so the system improves over time.
acceptance_criteria:
- /app/batches lists pending batches with timestamp, note count, op count
- Detail view shows each proposed op with accept/reject/edit controls
- Approved ops commit via existing graph mutation API
- Rejected/edited ops persist with reason metadata for model feedback
- Empty state when no pending batches

title: Batch draft generator: configurable provider + OpenAI batch client
description:
Given a batch context packet (from the context builder), call Claude to produce a structured set of proposed graph operations: new nodes, new edges, claim updates, suggested links between notes and existing graph entities, and proposed multi-note merges (e.g. three gel photos -> one observation).

Output is a structured JSON proposal stored as a 'pending batch' record for the review UI. No commits happen ? only proposals.
acceptance_criteria:
- Given a context packet, returns a structured proposal set (typed schema)
- Supports multi-note merge proposals
- Supports link proposals (note -> question/session/dataset)
- Stores result as a pending batch with full traceability back to source notes
- Failure modes (model timeout, invalid JSON) handled with retries + dead-letter
notes: Closed with the provider abstraction (GraphDraftClient Protocol + make_graph_draft_client factory) and the OpenAIGraphDraftClient.draft_from_batch method landed in commit 1872618. Settings gain graph_draft_provider (default openai). Persistence of batch proposals as pending review records, plus retry/dead-letter handling, are split out into lab-tracker-8ay because they touch the data model and warrant a separate commit. Provider clients for Claude and Gemini are tracked as lab-tracker-dvt and lab-tracker-z66.
close_reason: Closed

title: Batch context builder: assemble notes + graph slice for the model
description:
Build the context packet the model sees when drafting a daily batch. Should include: the full set of unprocessed notes (text, transcripts, image references), the relevant slice of the graph (projects/questions/sessions touched by those notes, plus their immediate neighbors), and any prior batch decisions on related entities.

This is what differentiates the daily batch from per-note drafting ? the model can see multiple related notes together and propose merges/relationships it couldn't see one at a time.
acceptance_criteria:
- Given a set of staged notes, returns a context packet with: notes payload, relevant graph subgraph, recent related decisions
- Context size bounded (paginated or truncated with priority signals if oversized)
- Tested with synthetic batches of varying size and graph density
- Output schema documented so the draft generator can consume it
close_reason: Closed

title: Daily batch runner: scheduled, idempotent draft job
description:
Add a scheduled job that runs once a day (configurable cron), collects all notes with status='staged' that arrived since the last successful run, and kicks off the batch context builder + draft generator.

Must be idempotent: re-running the same window must not produce duplicate batches. Should record run start/end, window covered, notes included, and outcome (success/error) for observability.
acceptance_criteria:
- Cron-style scheduler registers a daily job (default 06:00 local lab time, configurable)
- Job collects staged notes since last successful run watermark
- Idempotent: re-running same window does not create duplicate batches
- Run history persisted with window, note count, status, errors
- Manual 'run now' trigger available for admins/dev

title: Device-bound auth (passkey or long-lived device token) for phone
description:
Username + password on a phone keyboard is the single worst friction point. After the first desktop login, the user should pair their phone once (QR code from desktop, magic link, or WebAuthn passkey enrollment) and never type a password on the phone again.

Token lives in IndexedDB scoped to the installed PWA. Revocable from a 'My devices' page on desktop. No biometric requirement at this stage ? long-lived bearer token is acceptable for the trust model (single-user lab notebook).
design: Two options to evaluate: (a) WebAuthn passkey ? most secure, supported on modern iOS/Android, requires platform authenticator UX; (b) QR-code pair flow ? desktop generates a short-lived enrollment URL with embedded device-token signing material, phone scans, stores long-lived token. Option (b) is simpler to ship; option (a) is the long-term right answer. Pick one and document the reason.
acceptance_criteria:
- After first pairing, phone capture works without entering credentials
- Device tokens revocable from a desktop 'My devices' view
- Tokens scoped so they can call /notes/quick-capture and the share-target handler, nothing destructive
- Decision recorded for passkey vs. QR pair flow with rationale
close_reason: Closed

title: Add POST /notes/quick-capture minimal-payload endpoint
description:
The existing POST /notes/upload-file requires project_id and pushes many optional fields through the same path. Phone capture needs a stricter, leaner endpoint: accept an asset (image, audio, or text) plus an optional project_id (falls back to user's device-default project), nothing else.

All linking (question, session, dataset, analysis, claim) is deferred to the daily draft review (lab-tracker-cw3). The endpoint should return 202 Accepted with the staged note id; the client treats success as 'queued for daily review'.
acceptance_criteria:
- New route POST /notes/quick-capture accepts multipart asset + optional project_id
- Falls back to per-user device-default project when project_id omitted
- Returns 202 with note id; sets status='staged' for the daily batch to pick up
- Tests cover image, audio, and text-only variants
- Existing /notes/upload-file remains for desktop full-form flow
close_reason: Closed

title: Register Web Share Target for OS share-sheet capture
description:
Add a share_target entry to manifest.json so the installed PWA appears in the iOS/Android share sheet. When the user shares a photo from the Camera app, the OS routes it to a dedicated handler URL (e.g. /app/share-target) that ingests the file and forwards to the quick-capture endpoint.

This is the single biggest UX win on phone: zero-tap-to-Lab-Tracker from any app that can share an image.
acceptance_criteria:
- manifest.json declares share_target with accept=image/*,audio/*
- Handler route receives shared file via POST multipart and forwards to quick-capture
- Installed PWA appears in iOS and Android share sheets
- End-to-end: photo in Camera -> Share -> Lab Tracker -> staged note visible in app
close_reason: Closed

title: Add service worker for app shell cache and upload retry queue
description:
Register a service worker that (1) caches the app shell (HTML, app.js, styles.css, icons) so the app loads offline, and (2) intercepts POSTs to the quick-capture endpoint, queues failed uploads in IndexedDB, and retries them when connectivity returns.

This is what makes capture survive the network dropping in a microscope room or basement lab. Without it, a failed upload is a lost note.
acceptance_criteria:
- Service worker registers on first visit and caches app shell
- App loads fully offline after first visit
- Failed POST to /notes/quick-capture is queued in IndexedDB with full payload
- Queued uploads retry on 'online' event and on next app open
- UI shows pending unsynced count
close_reason: Closed

title: Add web app manifest with icons for PWA install
description:
Add a manifest.json (name, short_name, icons at 192/512, theme_color, background_color, start_url=/app/capture, display=standalone) and link it from index.html. Generate or commit app icons. This is the prerequisite that lets iOS/Android offer 'Add to Home Screen' and launch the app fullscreen like a native app.

Without this, none of the other PWA work (share target, install prompt) functions.
acceptance_criteria:
- manifest.json served at a stable URL, referenced from index.html
- Icons at minimum 192x192 and 512x512 committed
- 'Add to Home Screen' offered on iOS Safari and Android Chrome
- Installed app launches at /app/capture in standalone mode
close_reason: Closed

title: Epic: Daily AI graph-draft batch
description:
Replace per-note draft generation with a once-a-day batch. Drafting on every upload thrashes context and wastes model calls on incomplete information; a daily cadence lets the model see accumulated notes together, dedupe, propose coherent multi-note merges, and produce a single review queue.

Goal: each day, a scheduled job collects all notes that landed since the last run, builds a graph-aware context packet covering them, asks Claude to propose graph operations (new nodes, edges, claim updates), and stores the result as a pending batch in the existing graph-draft review UI. The human reviews once per day instead of per note.

Pairs with the 'PWA capture-first phone workflow' epic: capture cheaply through the day, review proposals in one sitting.
design: Batch is the unit of review, not the individual note. Runner is idempotent (re-runnable on the same window without duplicates). Context builder pulls unprocessed notes + the relevant graph slice (projects/questions touched). Draft generator can propose merges across multiple notes (e.g. three photos from the same gel become one observation). Review UI extends the existing graph-draft card pattern to a batch container.
acceptance_criteria:
- Scheduled runner executes daily, idempotently, with configurable window
- Batch context builder collects all notes since last successful run + relevant graph slice
- Claude draft generator produces a structured proposal set covering the batch
- Pending batches appear in the review UI with per-operation accept/reject
- Approved operations commit through the existing graph mutation path
- Rejected/edited operations are recorded for future model feedback
- Notification surfaces when a new batch is ready for review

title: Epic: PWA capture-first phone workflow
description:
Make phone note capture nearly effortless. The current /app/capture screen requires login, mandatory project selection, and a network round-trip before anything is saved ? too much friction for one-handed bench work.

Goal: a user takes a photo with their phone's normal Camera app, hits Share, picks Lab Tracker, and the note is staged. No browser open, no login each time, no fields required beyond the captured asset.

This requires turning the existing static-bundle frontend into a Progressive Web App: web app manifest (Add to Home Screen), service worker (offline asset cache + upload retry queue), Web Share Target (OS share-sheet integration), and a device-bound auth path (passkey or long-lived device token) that eliminates the password prompt on phone. The note API also needs a minimal-payload quick-capture endpoint that accepts asset + device-default project and defers all linking to the daily draft review.

Pairs with the 'Daily AI graph-draft batch' epic: capture cheaply now, AI proposes structured graph updates once a day for human review.
design: Phone capture flow target: Camera -> Share Sheet -> Lab Tracker -> staged. <3 taps, works offline. Auth via device-bound passkey/token in IndexedDB, not username/password. Quick-capture endpoint accepts only asset + project; everything else (question/session/dataset links) gets proposed by the daily batch and confirmed in the review card.
acceptance_criteria:
- manifest.json served with icons, theme, start URL
- Service worker caches the app shell and queues failed uploads with retry
- Web Share Target registered so OS share sheet routes photos to a capture endpoint
- POST /notes/quick-capture accepts minimal payload (asset + project_id), returns 202 if queued
- Device-bound auth path lets a phone authenticate without typing a password on each visit
- Offline capture survives a network drop and syncs when connectivity returns

title: Clarify and harden MCP note creation validation for status and metadata
description:
While recording the 2026-04-28 temporal-gradient projector titration analysis through the Lab Tracker MCP connector, `lab_tracker_create_note` accepted only a reduced payload after two confusing validation failures.

Observed behavior:
- Creating a note with `status="active"` failed, while the analogous question flow accepts `active`. This is technically consistent with `NoteStatus` (`staged`, `committed`, `archived`), but the MCP tool exposes `status` as a free string and the skill/API docs do not make the note-specific allowed values obvious.
- Creating a note with structured metadata failed unless all metadata values were strings. `NoteCreate.metadata` is typed as `dict[str, str]`, so Pydantic rejects non-string JSON values before the request reaches `_normalize_note_metadata`, even though the service normalizer is written to coerce non-string values to strings.
- The successful fallback was to create the note with `status="staged"` and no metadata, which avoided data loss but made the assistant workflow more brittle and less informative.

Concrete example context:
- Project: `b97935f1-42c6-475d-b35f-0e23607d11e6`
- Successful fallback note: `4dc2ec50-7781-475d-ba3d-b89c0c79895b`
- MCP tool: `lab_tracker_create_note`
- Relevant code paths noticed during triage: `src/lab_tracker/schemas.py` (`NoteCreate.metadata: dict[str, str]`, `status: NoteStatus | None`), `src/lab_tracker/mcp_server.py` (`lab_tracker_create_note(status: str | None, metadata: dict[str, str] | None)`), and `src/lab_tracker/services/shared.py` (`_normalize_note_metadata` coerces values).

Why this matters:
Assistant clients will naturally use project/question status vocabulary and structured provenance metadata. The current behavior requires hidden knowledge of note-specific status values and silently discourages preserving useful machine-readable provenance on notes.
acceptance_criteria:
- `lab_tracker_create_note` docs/schema expose the allowed note statuses (`staged`, `committed`, `archived`) clearly, or the MCP layer rejects invalid statuses with a targeted error before the generic API failure.
- Decide whether note metadata should accept JSON scalar values and normalize them, or remain string-only; make the API schema, service normalizer, MCP type hints, and docs agree.
- Add or update tests for MCP note creation covering invalid note status and metadata values with at least one non-string scalar.
- Update the Lab Tracker skill/docs so assistant clients know the note status vocabulary and metadata contract.
close_reason: Clarified note status validation and aligned scalar metadata handling across API, MCP, tests, docs, and installed skills.
